newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures widen gains but lag behind NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures widen gains but lag behind NY.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures gained some upward momentum to end Monday sharply up but the market failed to keep pace with racing New York arabica futures amid news of a planned strike by Brazilian port workers.
London's benchmark May broke through the immediate $1,655 a tonne hurdle to peak at $1,660 in the afternoon on New York's rally. But it retreated back to end the day at $1,652, still a $55 gain.
Traders said London's reluctance to chase surging arabicas which hit a new life-high at 184.80 basis May reflecting the less encouraging fundamental outlook for the robustas.

"The arabicas are under-supplied while robustas are oversupplied," said one, saying that arabica supplies could remain tight for the rest of the year. On the contrary, robusta is being pressured by large harvests from Vietnam, Cameroon, Ivory Coast and possibly Indonesia.
May/May arbitrage, already at historically high levels, widened further to 108 U.S. cents a lb from 102 at Friday's finish.
New York values were given a lift on news workers at Brazil's key Parangua port planned to go on strike on March 5.
A union spokesman told Reuters the port was already operating at only 50 percent of normal capacity, but traders and port officials insisted that operations were normal.

U.S. Merrill Lynch forecast pegging Colombia's 1996/97 coffee crop at between 9.4 million and 10.5 million bags was seen at the lower end of trade expectation but traders said the news had little impact so far.
London's market gapped higher at the opening as expected and the prices were later supported by short-covering on March which enters the month-long notice period on Monday.
The March firmness helped narrow nearby March/May and May/July spread to level money at one stage.
LIFFE said 761 originals were tendered on Monday. There were no re-tenders.
Overall volume reached 6,622 lots. The options pit also saw brisk activity, dominated by May $1,650 and $1,700 calls.
Technically, analysts said May could now aim for an upside target of $1,720 scored on February 13 -- the contract's highest level since last June. Support is seen at $1,550.
Friday's U.S. Commitment of Traders report showed again a sizeable net speculative long position of 14,034 lots.

"At the moment, the speculators and funds are probably on the right side of the market," said one. "But if the market turns around to say below 170 on March (in New York), they may cut their positions."
